topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Geometric Meaning of a Matrix
lecture_lines: A matrix is a machine transforming space.
Columns reveal where basis vectors land.
Example: A rotation matrix shifts basis.
animations: Fade in a 2D plane with unit basis vectors i_hat and j_hat in #FFFFFF.
Animate i_hat and j_hat moving to new columns as vectors.
Show a rotation matrix shifting i_hat and j_hat visibly in #FFD700.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition
lecture_lines: Composition means applying transformations in sequence.
First B, then A, is applied.
animations: Display two distinct transformation grids A and B in #00FFFF and #FF4500.
Represent the composition A(B(v)) as two sequential mapping functions.
Show vector v transforming under B, then resulting vector transforming under A.

sections.title: Deriving the Matrix Product
lecture_lines: Composition A(B(v)) equals one matrix C.
Matrix product C equals A times B.
Observe basis paths through B then A.
This determines the product's column values.
animations: Combine A and B into a single composite transformation operator C.
Animate the matrix product C = AB appearing in #FFFF00.
Trace i_hat through B to get a vector, then through A.
Map the result of the trace to the first column of C.
Repeat the trace for j_hat to complete the columns of C.

sections.title: Visualizing Non-Commutativity
lecture_lines: Rotate then stretch differs from stretch then rotate.
Final grid orientation confirms this difference.
animations: Display two grids showing different final orientations for AB vs BA.
Animate a rotation then stretch, highlighting the resulting grid state.
Animate a stretch then rotation, contrasting with the first state.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Multiplication acts as a transformation shortcut.
Combine operations into one final matrix.
animations: Show matrix multiplication as a compressed shortcut to complex transformations.
Visualize multiple matrices collapsing into a single final matrix.
Show a computational efficiency gain icon with a fast-forward symbol.
